name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description:
Information Systems - academic year 23/24
Course Project
Scenario

La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of materials and products for the home. To improve the efficiency of its operations and the service to customers, the company is re-designing its information system. The details follow.

La Reine Marlene has a wide network of suppliers. The suppliers of La Reine Marlene will have to register in the system, providing their credentials and company details, including VAT number, address and the IBAN for payments. Registered suppliers can make proposals of their own products by entering in the system the following information for each product: category, sale price (the one that La Reine Marlene must pay to the supplier), availability, photo, description, guaranteed delivery time. The product categories are 16: Garden, Bathroom, Air Conditioning, Lighting, Decoration, Flooring, Doors and Windows, Carpentry, Kitchen, Storage, Tools, Electricity, Construction, Paints, Hardware, Furniture. Once a proposal has been entered, the supplier can no longer modify it until they receive a response notification.

When a supplier enters a proposal, the administration department of La Reine Marlene receives a message notifying the presence of a new proposal from the suppliers. At that point, it must verify the proposal and select one of the following options: Order accepted, Revisions requested, Order rejected. If the order is accepted, a separate order management process will start, to which the information on the price to be displayed in the store is added, so that this information will already be available in the subsequent processes. If instead revisions have been requested, they must be made explicit in a comment: at that point the supplier receives a notification and has 5 working days to modify the proposal, entering reply comments, and re-submit it. If the proposal has been modified within the 5 working days, then the proposal evaluation process restarts, otherwise the proposal is deleted from the system and the supplier notified. The administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours about the presence of a proposal that is waiting to be validated. A proposal that has not been verified within 10 working days is automatically rejected, and a specific message is sent to the supplier.

Once the products ordered from the suppliers are shipped and arrive at the destination La Reine Marlene site (there are dozens of them throughout Italy), they are entered in the inventory of all the products available in the store (La Reine Marlene has no warehouse: any available product is on display). Each product is catalogued according to its category, available quantity and location in the store. The location in the store is entered directly by the goods receiving staff: when an order is delivered, the staff members must verify each product. If there are no problems, the operator confirms the product and the system proposes a list of possible placements: the location is chosen, and the product is physically handed over to whoever will take care of its placement in the store and of printing the price to be displayed. Should there be problems with any product, the operator reports it by entering a comment and the product does not enter the store. At the end of these operations of verification of an order arrival, the operator closes the procedure and a new process starts, managed by the order department: if all the products have been accepted, the order is concluded and the payment sent. Otherwise, the order is updated and a new arrival that completes it is awaited. In both cases specific messages are sent to the supplier.

The system keeps track of stock in real time. An automatic notification is sent to the order department when a product reaches a critical reorder level (where it is specified). The administrators, in fact, can schedule automatic reordering and replenishment actions for specific products, in order to maintain an optimal inventory. In case of automatic reordering, a message is sent to the pre-established supplier, who has two working days to confirm acceptance of the order. In the absence of critical thresholds and of the related automation, the new order is managed by the order department with a separate process.

Customers looking for materials for the home can purchase the products both through the physical store and through the online store. In the online store, customers who have registered on the site can browse the digital catalogue, specify the desired products and quantities and complete the order. The system automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs. Customers can choose among different payment options: credit card (Visa or Mastercard), Paypal, Satispay, the La Reine Marlene purchasing card, or immediate online bank transfer with the affiliated banks. Once the order is paid, the system keeps track of deliveries in real time. Customers receive a link by email through which they can follow the status of their shipments. In addition, those who have given consent to the use of the mobile phone number will receive notifications on updates to delivery times. Once the product arrives at its destination, the order is tracked as concluded. Deliveries are managed by partner companies, and each online purchase is randomly assigned to a shipping carrier. Consider that the online store is also accessible through a dedicated app: the operations and procedures are the same as those of the site.

La Reine Marlene offers a complete customer service through the information system. Customers can ask questions, request assistance or make complaints directly through the system. Support tickets are automatically assigned to a customer service agent. Every time a ticket is assigned, the agent receives a notification and has 24 hours to respond (if this does not happen, the ticket is reassigned to a new operator, and the statistics updated). The customer is informed upon receipt of the reply message, and has five working days to respond: otherwise, the ticket is considered closed.

Finally, the system collects data on orders, sales, inventory, customer support. These data are used to analyze performance and make strategic decisions.
highLevelGoals: Suppliers aim to efficiently submit product proposals, including all necessary details, to La Reine Marlene for consideration.
Suppliers aim to timely modify and resubmit proposals when revisions are requested, ensuring their products remain in consideration.
Suppliers aim to receive clear and timely notifications regarding the status of their proposals (accepted, rejected, revisions requested) to manage their business effectively.
Suppliers aim to receive automatic confirmations for reorders to streamline their order fulfillment process.
The Administration Department Staff aims to efficiently evaluate supplier product proposals, making timely decisions to accept, reject, or request revisions.
The Administration Department Staff aims to accurately manage and add the display price for accepted products to ensure correct pricing in the store.
The Administration Department Staff aims to make decisions on proposals within specified timeframes to avoid automatic rejections and maintain supplier relationships.
The Goods Receiving Staff aims to accurately verify delivered products against orders to ensure quality and correctness.
The Goods Receiving Staff aims to efficiently assign store locations for accepted products and ensure their accurate entry into the inventory system.
The Goods Receiving Staff aims to effectively report any problems with delivered products, preventing faulty items from entering the store inventory.
The Order Department Staff aims to timely conclude orders and process payments to suppliers once all products have been accepted.
The Order Department Staff aims to efficiently manage automatic reordering and replenishment actions to maintain optimal inventory levels and prevent stockouts.
The Order Department Staff aims to effectively update and manage orders that arrive partially, awaiting subsequent deliveries to complete them.
Customers aim to seamlessly browse the digital catalogue, select desired products and quantities, and complete orders through the online store or app.
Customers aim to have a variety of secure payment options to choose from, ensuring convenience and flexibility during checkout.
Customers aim to track the status of their orders and deliveries in real-time, receiving timely updates via email or mobile notifications.
Customers aim to efficiently ask questions, request assistance, or make complaints directly through the system, expecting timely responses.
Customer Service Agents aim to timely respond to assigned support tickets, resolving customer questions, assistance requests, and complaints within service level agreements.
Customer Service Agents aim to effectively manage their assigned support tickets, ensuring that customer responses are received and tickets are closed appropriately.
lowLevelGoals: The system shall allow the Supplier to submit a new product proposal with all required details (product name, description, category, price, images, etc.).
The system shall allow the Supplier to upload and attach multiple images to a product proposal.
The system shall allow the Supplier to specify the proposed pricing details for a product, including wholesale price and suggested retail price.
The system shall allow the Supplier to retrieve and modify the details of an existing product proposal that has been flagged for revision.
The system shall allow the Supplier to resubmit a modified product proposal for re-evaluation.
The system shall send an automated notification (e.g., email, in-app alert) to the Supplier when the status of their product proposal changes (e.g., accepted, rejected, revisions requested).
The system shall allow the Supplier to view the current status and any associated comments or reasons for a proposal's status change.
The system shall send an automated confirmation to the Supplier upon the generation of a reorder for their products.
The system shall allow the Supplier to view the details of an automatic reorder, including product quantities and expected delivery dates.
The system shall allow the Administration Department Staff to retrieve a list of pending product proposals submitted by suppliers.
The system shall allow the Administration Department Staff to view all details of a specific product proposal, including product information, images, and proposed pricing.
The system shall allow the Administration Department Staff to mark a product proposal as 'accepted'.
The system shall allow the Administration Department Staff to mark a product proposal as 'rejected' and provide a reason.
The system shall allow the Administration Department Staff to mark a product proposal as 'revisions requested' and provide specific feedback to the supplier.
The system shall allow the Administration Department Staff to add the final display price for an accepted product.
The system shall allow the Administration Department Staff to update the display price for an existing product.
The system shall display a list of pending proposals along with their submission dates and remaining time until automatic rejection.
The system shall send automated alerts to the Administration Department Staff for proposals nearing their decision deadline.
The system shall allow the Goods Receiving Staff to scan or manually enter product details from a delivery and compare them against the corresponding purchase order.
The system shall allow the Goods Receiving Staff to record the exact quantity of each product received during a delivery.
The system shall allow the Goods Receiving Staff to assign a specific store location (e.g., aisle, shelf number) to each received product.
The system shall automatically update the inventory levels for products once they are marked as received and assigned a location.
The system shall allow the Goods Receiving Staff to report issues with delivered products, such as damage, incorrect items, or quantity discrepancies, and attach relevant details.
The system shall generate a formal report for reported product issues, including details for further action (e.g., return to supplier, claim processing).
The system shall allow the Order Department Staff to mark an order as 'complete' once all products associated with it have been received and verified.
The system shall allow the Order Department Staff to initiate payment processing to the supplier for a completed order.
The system shall continuously monitor inventory levels and identify products falling below predefined reorder thresholds.
The system shall automatically generate a reorder request for products when their inventory levels reach the reorder point.
The system shall allow the Order Department Staff to adjust reorder thresholds and quantities for specific products.
The system shall allow the Order Department Staff to update an order to reflect a partial delivery, indicating which items and quantities have arrived.
The system shall display a clear overview of orders with pending partial deliveries, including expected remaining items and delivery dates.
The system shall allow the Customer to browse products available in the digital catalogue, categorized and searchable.
The system shall allow the Customer to add desired products and specified quantities to a shopping cart.
The system shall allow the Customer to proceed from the shopping cart to the checkout process.
The system shall present the Customer with a variety of secure payment options (e.g., credit card, debit card, mobile payment, bank transfer) during checkout.
The system shall securely process the Customer's selected payment method for the order.
The system shall allow the Customer to view the current status of their order (e.g., 'processing', 'shipped', 'out for delivery') through the online store or app.
The system shall send automated notifications (e.g., email, SMS) to the Customer for significant updates to their order or delivery status.
The system shall allow the Customer to submit a question, assistance request, or complaint through a dedicated support interface.
The system shall allow the Customer to track the status of their submitted inquiries and view responses from customer service.
The system shall notify Customer Service Agents of new support tickets assigned to them.
The system shall allow the Customer Service Agent to view all details of an assigned support ticket, including customer message and history.
The system shall allow the Customer Service Agent to compose and send a response to a customer's inquiry within the support ticket.
The system shall allow the Customer Service Agent to update the status of a support ticket (e.g., 'in progress', 'awaiting customer response', 'resolved').
The system shall allow the Customer Service Agent to close a support ticket once the customer's issue has been resolved.
The system shall display a list of all support tickets currently assigned to the Customer Service Agent, with filtering and sorting options.
